nodes.name: Non-local operator with variable order $\LL$
nodes.statement: Let $\LL$ be a non-local operator with variable order given by \begin{equation} \LL f(x)=\int_{\R^d}\big(f(x+z)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x), z\rangle \I_{\{|z|\le 1\}}\big) \frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz,\quad f \in C_c^2(\R^d), \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The variable-order non-local generator $\LL$ with jump kernel $\kappa(x,z)/|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}$.

nodes.name: Order of the non-local operator at a point
nodes.statement: For this reason, we call $\alpha(x)$ the order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \R^d$.
nodes.genus: order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \R^d$

nodes.name: Ball $B(x_0,r)$
nodes.statement: For $x_0\in \R^d$ and $r>0$, define $B(x_0, r):=\{x\in \R^d: |x-x_0|< r_0\}$.

nodes.name: $C_{b,u}(\R^d)$
nodes.statement: Let $C_{b,u}(\R^d)$ denote the set of all bounded and uniformly continuous functions on $\R^d$.
nodes.genus: set of all bounded and uniformly continuous functions on $\R^d$

nodes.name: Feller process
nodes.statement: Recall that a Markov process on $\R^d$ is said to be a Feller process if its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped with the uniform norm.
differentia: its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped with the uniform norm

nodes.name: Strong Feller property
nodes.statement: A Markov process is said to have the strong Feller property if its transition semigroup maps bounded measurable functions to bounded continuous functions.
differentia: its transition semigroup maps bounded measurable functions to bounded continuous functions

nodes.name: Frozen-coefficient operator $\LL^y$
nodes.statement: For fixed $y \in \R^d$, define \begin{equation} \LL^y f(x):=\int_{\R^d}\big(f(x+z)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x), z \rangle\I_{\{|z|\le 1\}}\big)\frac{\K(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz. \end{equation} Then $ \LL^y$ is the generator of a pure jump symmetric L\'{e}vy process $X^y:=(X_t^y)_{t\ge 0}$ with jump measure $\nu^y(dz)=\frac{\K(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz$.
nodes.statement_short: $\LL^y$ freezes the coefficients of $\LL$ at $y$; it generates a pure-jump symmetric L\'evy process $X^y$.
nodes.genus: generator of a pure jump symmetric L\'{e}vy process $X^y:=(X_t^y)_{t\ge 0}$

nodes.name: Fundamental solution $p^y$ of $\LL^y$
nodes.statement: We denote the fundamental solution for $ \LL^y$ by $p^y:(0,\infty)\times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$, which is just the transition density of the process $X^y$. The fundamental solution $p^y$ satisfies that \begin{equation*} \frac{\partial p^y(t,x)}{\partial t}= \LL^yp^y(t,\cdot)(x) \quad \hbox{for every } (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \R^d. \end{equation*} We remark here that although the operator $ \LL^y$ is clearly well defined on $C_c^2(\R^d)$. It is also pointwisely well defined for the function $x\mapsto p^y(t, x)$; see the estimates in \cite[Theorem 2.4]{CZ}.
nodes.statement_short: $p^y$ is the heat kernel / transition density of the frozen L\'evy process $X^y$.
differentia: which is just the transition density of the process $X^y$

nodes.name: Second difference operators $\delta_f$ and $\delta_{p^y}$
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, we define for $ f:\R^d\rightarrow \R$, \begin{equation*} \delta_f(x;z):=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x), \quad \ x,z\in \R^d. \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \delta_{p^y}(t,x;z):=p^y(t,x+z)+p^y(t,x-z)-2p^y(t,x),\quad t\in (0,\infty),\ x,y,z\in \R^d. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Local sup/inf of the index function, $\overline{\A}(y;s)$ and $\underline{\A}(y;s)$
nodes.statement: For every $y \in \R^d$ and $s>0$, define $ \overline{\A}(y;s):=\sup\{\A(z): |z-y|\le s\}$ and $ \underline{\A}(y;s):=\inf\{\A(z): |z-y|\le s\}. $ For simplicity, we write $\overline \A(y;|x-y|)$ and $\underline{\A}(y;|x-y|)$ as $\overline{\A}(y;x)$ and $\underline{\A}(y;x)$, respectively.
nodes.genus: local supremum and infimum of the index function $\A$

nodes.name: The key comparison function $\rho_{\G,R}^{y,\beta}$
nodes.statement: For each fixed $y \in \R^d$, $\B \in [0,\infty)$, $\G\in \R$ and $R \in (0,\infty)$, we define a function $\rho_{\G,R}^{y,\beta}:(0,1]\times \R^d \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ as follows \begin{equation*} \rho_{\G,R}^{y,\beta}(t,x):=t^{\G}\big(|x|^{\beta}\wedge 1\big) \begin{cases} \big(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-(d+\A(y))},& |x|\le R,\\ |x|^{-(d+\A_1)},& |x|> R, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $\alpha(x)$ is the index function in \eqref{e1-1} and $\alpha_1$ is the lower bound of $\alpha (x)$ in \eqref{e1-3}. It is easy to see that for any $0<R_1\le R_2<\infty$, there is a constant $c>1$ such that $c^{-1}\rho_{\G,R_1}^{y,\beta}\le \rho^{y,\beta}_{\G,R_2}\le c\rho_{\G,R_1}^{y,\beta}$ for all $y\in \R^d$ and $\beta\in[0,\infty)$. Therefore, without loss of generality, we may and do assume that $R=1$ in the definition of $\rho_{\G,R}^{y,\beta},$ and we write $\rho_{\G,1}^{y,\beta}$ as $\rho_{\G}^{y,\beta}$, which is exactly the one defined by \eqref{e3-0}.
nodes.statement_short: $\rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ is the variable-order profile $t^{\gamma}(|x|^{\beta}\wedge1)$ times a stable-type kernel at index $\A(y)$, cut off at $|x|=1$.

nodes.name: Notation $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\asymp$, $\preceq$, $\succeq$
nodes.statement: For any $a,b\in \R_+$, $a\wedge b:=\min\{a,b\}$ and $a\vee b:=\max \{a,b\}.$ For every measurable function $f,g:(0,1]\times\R^d\times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$, the notation $f \asymp g$ means that there exists a constant $1\le c_0<\infty$ such that $c_0^{-1} g(t,x,y)\le f(t,x,y)\le c_0 g(t,x,y)$ for every $(t,x,y) \in (0,1]\times\R^d\times \R^d $, and the notation $f \p g$ (resp.\ $f \q g$) means that there exists a constant $0<c_1<\infty$ such that $f(t,x,y)\le c_1 g(t,x,y)$ (resp.\ $f(t,x,y)\ge c_1g(t,x,y)$) for every $(t,x,y) \in (0,1]\times\R^d\times \R^d $.
nodes.statement_short: Comparison notation: $\asymp$ two-sided comparability, $\preceq$/$\succeq$ one-sided comparability up to constants.

nodes.name: Modified comparison function $\tilde \rho_{\G,\e}^{y,\theta}$
nodes.statement: For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, $\G\in \R$, $\theta \in \R_+$ and $x, y \in \R^d$, define \begin{equation} \tilde \rho_{\G,\e}^{y,\theta }(t,x)=t^{\G}(|x|^{\theta}\wedge 1) \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x|\le 1,\\ \frac{1}{|x|^{d+\A_1-\varepsilon}},& |x|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A variant of $\rho$ with the far-field exponent relaxed from $d+\A_1$ to $d+\A_1-\varepsilon$.
nodes.genus: comparison function of the same shape as $\rho$

nodes.name: Iterated kernels $q_n$
nodes.statement: For this, we first define $q_n(t,x,y)$ inductively by \begin{equation} q_n(t,x,y):=\int_0^t\int_{\R^d}q_0(t-s,x,z)q_{n-1}(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds,\ n\ge1,\ t\in(0,1]. \end{equation}
nodes.genus: inductively defined space-time convolution iterate of $q_0$

nodes.name: Splitting $\LL^y=\LL_{\K_1/2}^y+\LL_{\wh \K}^y$
nodes.statement: We write $ \LL^y=\LL_{{\K_1}/{2}}^y+\LL_{\wh \K}^y$ with \begin{align*} \LL_{{\K_1}/{2}}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\K_1}{2}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\A(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\R^d),\\ \LL_{\wh \K}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\wh \K(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\A(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\R^d), \end{align*} where $\K_1>0$ is the constant in \eqref{e1-2}, $\wh \K(y,z):=\K(y,z)-\K_1/2$ and $$\delta_f(x;z)=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x).$$
nodes.statement_short: Peel off a constant multiple of the rotationally symmetric $\A(y)$-stable generator from $\LL^y$.

nodes.name: The convolution term $\phi(t,s,x,y)$
nodes.statement: For every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y \in \R^d$, define \begin{equation*} \phi(t,s,x,y):=\int_{\R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz, \end{equation*} where $q(t,x,y)$ is constructed in Proposition \ref{p3-1}.
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution

nodes.name: Jumping kernel $J(x,y)$
nodes.statement: $$J(x,y):=\frac{\K(x,y-x)}{|y-x|^{d+\A(x)}},\quad x,y \in \R^d.$$
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution

nodes.name: Hitting and exit times $\sigma_D$, $\tau_D$
nodes.statement: For any subset $D\subseteq \R^d$, define \begin{equation*} \sigma_{D}:=\inf\{t \ge 0: X_t \in D\},\qquad \tau_D:=\inf\{t \ge 0: X_t \notin D\}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution

nodes.name: H\"older spaces $C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\R^d)$ and $C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\R^d)$
nodes.statement: Denote by $C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\R^d)$ the set of bounded H\"{o}lder continuous functions, and by $C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\R^d)$ the set of bounded twice differentiable functions whose second derivatives are uniformly H\"{o}lder continuous.
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.genus: sets of bounded H\"{o}lder continuous functions
differentia: bounded twice differentiable functions whose second derivatives are uniformly H\"{o}lder continuous

nodes.name: The common H\"older exponent $\beta_0$
nodes.statement: Set $\beta_0= \beta_1\wedge \beta_2$. Clearly \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2} hold with $\beta_0$ in place of $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$, respectively.
nodes.genus: minimum of the two H\"older exponents

nodes.name: Abbreviation $f(x\pm y)$
nodes.statement: For simplicity, we use the following abbreviation for a function $f$: $$ f(x\pm y):= f(x+y) + f(x-y). $$

nodes.name: Bounds and H\"older continuity of the index function $\alpha$
nodes.statement: where $\alpha:\R^d \rightarrow (0,2)$ is a measurable function such that \begin{equation} \begin{split} & 0<\alpha_1\le \alpha(x) \le \alpha_2<2 \quad \hbox{for } x \in \R^d,\\ & |\A(x)-\A(y)|\le c_1(|x-y|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1) \quad \hbox{for } x,y\in \R^d, \end{split} \end{equation} for some constants $c_1\in(0,\infty)$ and $\beta_1\in(0,1]$,
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha$ is measurable with $0<\alpha_1\le\alpha\le\alpha_2<2$ and is $\beta_1$-H\"older up to distance one.

nodes.name: Symmetry, two-sided bounds and H\"older continuity of $\kappa$
nodes.statement: $\kappa:\R^d\times \R^d \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a measurable function satisfying \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \K(x,z)=\K(x,-z) \quad \hbox{for } x,z \in \R^d,\\ & 0<\K_1\le \K(x,z)\le \K_2<\infty \quad \hbox{for } x,z\in \R^d,\\ & |\K(x,z)-\K(y,z)|\le c_2(|x-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1) \quad \hbox{for } x,y,z\in \R^d, \end{split} \end{equation} for some constants $c_2\in(0,\infty)$ and $\beta_2 \in (0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa$ is symmetric in $z$, bounded between $\K_1$ and $\K_2$, and $\beta_2$-H\"older in $x$.

nodes.name: Standing hypotheses for the lower bound estimates
nodes.statement: Throughout this part, we will always suppose that either of two conditions below is satisfied: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. \item [(2)] $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, and $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<\B_0^{**}/{\A_2},$ where $\B_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap(0,\alpha_2/2).$ \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: Either $\K$ is $z$-free, or $\K$ depends on $z$ with small index oscillation $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}$.

nodes.name: Construction and two-sided bounds of a genuine fundamental solution for non-constant $\A(x)$
nodes.statement: When $\A(x)$ is not a constant, how can we construct a fundamental solution of $\LL$ that really satisfies the parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} below? What are upper and lower bound estimates for this solution (if it exists)? We point out that it had not been established that, even under additional smoothness assumptions on $\alpha (x)$ and $\kappa (x)$, the heat kernel constructed in \cite{Kol} by Duhamel formula is actually a solution to the equation \eqref{t1-1-1}.
nodes.statement_short: For non-constant $\A(x)$, can one build a fundamental solution that truly solves the parabolic equation, and bound it above and below?

nodes.name: Existence of a strong Markov process associated with $\LL$ when $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$
nodes.statement: When $\A(x)$ is not a constant and $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, is there a strong Markov process associated with $\LL$? In literature, the existence of strong Markov process was always assumed a priori in the study of regularity of harmonic functions and elliptic Harnack inequalities for such non-local operator $\LL$, see \cite{BK1,BK2, LW} for examples.
nodes.statement_short: Is there a strong Markov process associated with $\LL$ when $\A(x)$ varies and $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$?

nodes.name: Local regularity of the fundamental solution in terms of $\A(x_0)$
nodes.statement: In existing literature, regularity for the solution to parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} associated with $\LL$ usually depends on the uniform bounds $\A_1$ and $\A_2$ in \eqref{e1-3}. Can one establish regularity of the fundamental solution in some neighborhood of $x_0$ (such as gradient estimate) in terms of $\A(x_0)$ under some special settings?
nodes.statement_short: Can regularity near $x_0$ be expressed through $\A(x_0)$ instead of the global bounds $\A_1,\A_2$?

nodes.name: Second-difference representation of $\LL^w p^y$
nodes.statement: Then, for every $x,y,w\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \LL^w p^y(t,\cdot)(x)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\R^d}\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)\frac{\K(w,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(w)}}\,dz. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\LL^w p^y(t,\cdot)(x)$ equals one half the $\delta_{p^y}$-integral against the frozen kernel at $w$.

nodes.name: Levi's method ansatz and the Volterra equation for $q$
nodes.statement: According to the Levi's method (cf. \cite[pp.\ 310--311]{Fi}), we look for the fundamental solution to \eqref{t1-1-1} of the following form: \begin{equation} \begin{split} & p(t,x,y)=p^y(t,x-y)+\int_0^t\int_{\R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds, \end{split} \end{equation} where $q(t,x,y)$ solves \begin{equation} q(t,x,y)=q_0(t,x,y)+\int_0^t\int_{\R^d}q_0(t-s,x,z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds \end{equation} with $ q_0(t,x,y)=( \LL^x- \LL^y)p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y). $
nodes.statement_short: Levi ansatz: $p=p^y+p^z*q$, with $q$ solving a Volterra equation driven by $q_0=(\LL^x-\LL^y)p^y$.

nodes.name: Principal-value (symmetric) form of $\LL$
nodes.statement: Due to the symmetry assumption $\K(x,z)=\K(x,-z)$, it is easy to see that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \LL f(x)&=\lim_{\e \downarrow 0}\frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|>\e\}} \big(f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x)\big)\frac{\K(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz. \end{split} \end{equation} For simplicity, throughout this paper we write $\LL f(x)$ as \begin{equation*} \LL f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\R^d} \big(f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x)\big)\frac{\K(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz. \end{equation*} Note that the above integral is absolutely convergent for bounded $C^2$ functions.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry of $\K$ in $z$ lets $\LL$ be written as a half second-difference integral, absolutely convergent on bounded $C^2$ functions.
assumptions: Due to the symmetry assumption $\K(x,z)=\K(x,-z)$
conclusions: it is easy to see that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \LL f(x)&=\lim_{\e \downarrow 0}\frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|>\e\}} \big(f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x)\big)\frac{\K(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz. \end{split} \end{equation} For simplicity, throughout this paper we write $\LL f(x)$ as \begin{equation*} \LL f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\R^d} \big(f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x)\big)\frac{\K(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz. \end{equation*} Note that the above integral is absolutely convergent for bounded $C^2$ functions.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (heat kernel for $\K(x,z)=\kappa(x)$ independent of $z$)
nodes.statement: Suppose that conditions \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2} hold. If $\K(x,z)= \kappa (x)$ is independent of $z$, then there exists a jointly continuous non-negative function $p:(0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+:=[0,\infty)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}=\LL p(t,\cdot,y)(x), \end{equation} and has the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)]{\bf (Upper bounds)}\,\, For every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1 =c_1(\A,\K,c_0)$ and $c_2 =c_2(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} {c_1}{t^{-{d/\A(x)}}},&\quad |x-y|< c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}}\wedge \frac{c_2t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},&\quad c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |x-y|< 1,\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&\quad|x-y|\ge 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $x_0\in\R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then there is a positive constant $c_3 =c_3(\A,\K,r_0)$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} \frac{c_3 t }{(t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}+|y-x_0|)^{d+\A(x_0)}},& |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_3 t }{|y-x_0|^{d+\A_1}},&|y-x_0|\ge {r_0}/{2}; \end{cases} \end{equation} \noindent {\bf (Lower bounds)}\,\, There exists a constant $c_4 =c_4(\A,\K)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\ge \frac{c_4t}{(t^{1/\A(x)}+|x-y|)^{d+\A(x)}}. \end{equation} \item[(ii)]{\bf (H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates)}\,\, For any $\G \in (0, \alpha_2]$, there exist positive constants $c_5 =c_5(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1=R_1(\A,\K,\G)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x, x', y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x', y)\big| &\le c_5 |x-x'|^{(\A(x)-\G)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_0}(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_0}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\gamma_0= {\G/(2\A_2)}$ and \begin{equation} \rho_{\G}^{y,\beta}(t,x)=t^{\G}(|x|^{\beta}\wedge 1) \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x|\le 1,\\ \frac{1}{|x|^{d+\A_1}},& |x|> 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If moreover $\tilde \B_0(x_0):=\big({\A_1\B_0}/{\A(x_0)})\wedge \A_1>1-\A(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. In this case, for every $\G>0$, $t\in(0,1]$ and $ y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_6 \, \rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\A(x_0)})+ (\B_0^*/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G}(t,x_0-y) \end{equation} for some $c_6 =c_6(\A,\K,\G,x_0)>0$, where $\B_0^*:=\B_0 \wedge\A_2$. \item[(iii)]{\bf (Chapman-Kolmogorov equation)} For every $s,t \in (0,1]$ with $s+t\le 1$, \begin{equation} \int_{\R^d}p(s,x,z)p(t,z,y)\,dz=p(s+t,x,y),\quad x,y\in \R^d. \end{equation} \item[(iv)]{\bf (Conservativeness)} For every $(t,x)\in (0,1]\times \R^d$, \begin{equation} \int_{\R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy=1. \end{equation} \item[(v)] {\bf (Strong continuity and generator)} For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\R^d)$, let $$u_f(t,x):=\int_{\R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.$$ Then \begin{equation} \LL u_f (t, \cdot) (x) \hbox{ exists pointwise}, \quad t \mapsto \LL u_f (t, ) (x) \hbox{ is continuous}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t} = \LL u_f(t,\cdot)(x), \quad t\in (0,1],\ x \in \R^d, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}|u_f(t,x)-f(x)|=0. \end{equation} For every $f \in C_{b,u}^2(\R^d):= C_{b,u}(\R^d)\cap C^2(\R^d)$, we also have \begin{equation} \frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\R^d} p(t,x,y)\LL f(y)\,dy,\quad t\in (0,1],\ x \in \R^d \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}\Big|\frac{1}{t}\cdot\big( u_f(t,x)-f(x)\big)-\LL f(x)\Big|=0. \end{equation} \item[(vi)] {\bf (Uniqueness)} Jointly continuous function $p(t, x, y)$ on $(0, 1]\times \R^d\times \R^d$ that is bounded for each $t>0$ and satisfies \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3} is unique. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 (heat kernel for general $\K(x,z)$ under small index oscillation)
nodes.statement: Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For general $\K (x, z)$ satisfying \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2}, if $ ({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}, $ there exists a jointly continuous non-negative function $p:(0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ such that all the conclusions in Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ hold except that the upper bounds \eqref{t1-1-4}-\eqref{t1-1-4a} in {\rm (i)} and H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a} in {\rm (ii)} are to be replaced by the following estimates. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)]{\bf (Upper bounds)}\,\, For any $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1 =c_1(\A,\K,c_0)>0$ and $c_2 =c_1(\A,\K,\G,c_0)>0$ such that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} {c_1}{t^{-{d/\A(x)}}},&\quad |x-y|< c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_1t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}} \wedge \frac{c_2t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},&\quad c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |x-y|< 1, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_1t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&\quad |x-y|\ge 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $x_0\in\R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for any $c_0>0$ there is a positive constant $c_3:=c_3(\A,\K,r_0,c_0)$ so that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} {c_3}{t^{-{d/\A (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_3 t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\A(x_0)}},& \quad c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}\le |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_3 t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\ge {r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(ii)] {\bf (H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates)}\,\, For every $\G \in (0, \A_1]$, there exist constants $c_5 =c_5(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1 =R_1(\A,\K,\G)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\le c_5|x-x'|^{(\A_1-\G)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:=1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})+({\G}/({2\A_2}))$. Let $\B_0^*$ and $\tilde \B_0(x_0)$ be the same constants in Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ $(ii)$. If moreover $\tilde \B_0(x_0)-({\A_1\A_2}/{\A(x_0)}) \big(({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1\big)>1-\A_1$ for some $x_0\in \R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. In this case, for every $\G>0$, there exists a constant $c_6:=c_6(\A,\K,\G, x_0)$ such that for all $ t\in (0,1]$ and $y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_6 \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\A_1)+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G_2}(t,x_0-y), \end{equation} where $\G_2=(\A_2/\A_1)-1+\G.$ \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 5.5 (maximum principle for the non-local parabolic equation)
nodes.statement: Let $u \in C_b([0,1]\times \R^d)$ be the solution of the following equation \begin{equation} {\partial_t u(t,x)}= \LL u(t,x),\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \R^d. \end{equation} Suppose \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}\big|u(t,x)-u(0,x)\big|=0, \end{equation} and for every $x \in \R^d$, $t \mapsto \LL u(t,x)$ is continuous in $t \in (0,1]$. Assume that there exists a function $\T(x)\in (0,1)$ such that $\inf_{x \in \R^d}\big(\T(x)+1-\A(x)\big)>0$ and for every $\e \in (0,1)$, \begin{equation} \sup_{t \in (\e,1)}\big|u(t,x)-u(t,x')\big|\le c_1(\e)|x-x'|^{\T(x)},\quad x,x'\in \R^d. \end{equation} Then for every $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation*} \sup_{x \in \R^d}u(t,x)\le \sup_{x \in \R^d}u(0,x). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: A bounded solution of $\partial_t u=\LL u$ that is continuous at $t=0$ and uniformly H\"older in $x$ with exponent $\T(x)>1-\A(x)$ obeys $\sup_x u(t,x)\le \sup_x u(0,x)$.
assumptions: Let $u \in C_b([0,1]\times \R^d)$ be the solution of the following equation \begin{equation} {\partial_t u(t,x)}= \LL u(t,x),\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \R^d. \end{equation} Suppose \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}\big|u(t,x)-u(0,x)\big|=0, \end{equation} and for every $x \in \R^d$, $t \mapsto \LL u(t,x)$ is continuous in $t \in (0,1]$. Assume that there exists a function $\T(x)\in (0,1)$ such that $\inf_{x \in \R^d}\big(\T(x)+1-\A(x)\big)>0$ and for every $\e \in (0,1)$, \begin{equation} \sup_{t \in (\e,1)}\big|u(t,x)-u(t,x')\big|\le c_1(\e)|x-x'|^{\T(x)},\quad x,x'\in \R^d. \end{equation}
conclusions: Then for every $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation*} \sup_{x \in \R^d}u(t,x)\le \sup_{x \in \R^d}u(0,x). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (mass of $\rho_0^{z,\beta}$ with $z$-dependent index)
nodes.statement: For every $\beta \in [0,\A_2)$, $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \int_{\R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\p \big(t^{(\beta/\A(x))-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\I_{\{\B=\A(x)\}}\big) \p t^{(\B/\A_2)-1}\vee 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $z$-integral of $\rho_0^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)$ is at most $t^{(\beta/\A(x))-1}\vee 1$ up to a logarithm.
assumptions: For every $\beta \in [0,\A_2)$, $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \int_{\R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\p \big(t^{(\beta/\A(x))-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\I_{\{\B=\A(x)\}}\big) \p t^{(\B/\A_2)-1}\vee 1. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (bounds for the auxiliary integrals $I_1,I_2,I_3$)
nodes.statement: For every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \R^d$, define \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|\le 1\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\A}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_2(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|>1\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\A}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_3(t,x,y):=&\int_{\R^d}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \left( \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\A}(y;x)}}\I_{\{|z|\le 1\}} +\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\A}(y;x)}}\I_{\{|z|> 1\}}\right)\,dz. \end{split} \end{equation} Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)$ such that for every $x,y,w \in \R^d$ and $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w) \le \begin{cases} c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big[1+|\log|w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|> {1}/{2}; \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} \begin{equation} I_2(t,x,y,w)\le \begin{cases} c_1\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w),\ & |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big(1+|\log|w||\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|>{1}/{2}; \end{cases} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} I_3(t,x,y)\le c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The three truncated jump integrals $I_1,I_2,I_3$ built from $\rho^{y,0}_1$ are dominated by $(1+|\log t|)t^{1-\overline{\A}(y;x)/\A(y)}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w)$ type expressions.
assumptions: For every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \R^d$, define \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|\le 1\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\A}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_2(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|>1\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\A}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_3(t,x,y):=&\int_{\R^d}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \left( \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\A}(y;x)}}\I_{\{|z|\le 1\}} +\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\A}(y;x)}}\I_{\{|z|> 1\}}\right)\,dz. \end{split} \end{equation}
conclusions: Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)$ such that for every $x,y,w \in \R^d$ and $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w) \le \begin{cases} c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big[1+|\log|w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|> {1}/{2}; \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} \begin{equation} I_2(t,x,y,w)\le \begin{cases} c_1\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w),\ & |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big(1+|\log|w||\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|>{1}/{2}; \end{cases} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} I_3(t,x,y)\le c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{-({\overline{\A}(y;x)}/{\A(y)})}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.6 (regularity estimates for $p^y$, from Chen--Zhang)
nodes.statement: The following statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z) =\K (x)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $j \in \mathbb{Z}_+:=\{0,1,\ldots\}$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, j)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla^j p^y(t,\cdot)(x)|\le c_1t\big(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-d-\A(y)-j}. \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\K(x,z)$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y,z \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p^y(t,x)\le c_2 \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x), \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)|\le c_2\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \begin{split} |p^y(t,x)-p^y(t,x')|&\le c_2\big[\big(t^{-{1/\A(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z)|& \le c_2 \big[\big(t^{-{1/\A(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]\\ &\quad\times\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')\big). \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Derivative bounds $|\nabla^j p^y|\p t(t^{1/\A(y)}+|x|)^{-d-\A(y)-j}$ for $z$-free $\K$, and $\rho$-type bounds on $p^y$, $\delta_{p^y}$ and their spatial increments in general.
assumptions: The following statements hold.
conclusions: \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z) =\K (x)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $j \in \mathbb{Z}_+:=\{0,1,\ldots\}$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, j)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla^j p^y(t,\cdot)(x)|\le c_1t\big(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-d-\A(y)-j}. \end{equation}

\item[(2)] For general $\K(x,z)$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y,z \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p^y(t,x)\le c_2 \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x), \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)|\le c_2\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \begin{split} |p^y(t,x)-p^y(t,x')|&\le c_2\big[\big(t^{-{1/\A(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z)|& \le c_2 \big[\big(t^{-{1/\A(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\A(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]\\ &\quad\times\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')\big). \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.7 (near-diagonal bound for $(\LL^x-\LL^y)p^y$ and $q_0$)
nodes.statement: For every $\G>0$, there exist constants $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)\in (0,{1}/{2})$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$ \begin{equation}\begin{split} &\big|\big( \LL^x - \LL^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big| \le c_1\big(|x-y|^{\B_0}\wedge 1\big) \cdot \begin{cases} t^{-\G}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w), &\ |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ (t^{-\G}+|\log |w||)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w),&\ |w|>{1}/{2}. \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} In particular, for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} \big|q_0(t,x,y)\big|\p \rho_{-\G}^{y,\B_0}(t,x-y). \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$, then there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K, \G, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$ with $|x-y_0|<r_0$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_2\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}}. \end{equation}
assumptions: For every $\G>0$, there exist constants $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)\in (0,{1}/{2})$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$
conclusions: \begin{equation}\begin{split} &\big|\big( \LL^x - \LL^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big| \le c_1\big(|x-y|^{\B_0}\wedge 1\big) \cdot \begin{cases} t^{-\G}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w), &\ |w|\le {1}/{2},\\ (t^{-\G}+|\log |w||)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w),&\ |w|>{1}/{2}. \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} In particular, for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} \big|q_0(t,x,y)\big|\p \rho_{-\G}^{y,\B_0}(t,x-y). \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$, then there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K, \G, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$ with $|x-y_0|<r_0$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_2\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (convolution inequality for $\rho$ with $z$-dependent index)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for all $0<s<t\le 1$ and $x,y \in \R^d$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d} \rho_{\T_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\T_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\p \Big[(t-s)^{\T_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A(x)\}}\big)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\T_1} s^{\T_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\T_1+[({\beta_1}/{\A(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1=\A(x)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\T_1}s^{\T_2+({\beta_2}/{\A(y)})\wedge 1 -1} \big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_2=\A(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for every $x,y \in \R^d$ and $0<s<t\le 1$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d} \rho_{\T_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\T_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\p \Big[(t-s)^{\T_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\T_1} s^{\T_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\T_1+[({\beta_1}/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1=\A_2\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\T_1}s^{\T_2+[({\beta_2}/{\A_2})\wedge 1] -1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation}\end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The space convolution $\rho_{\T_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,\cdot)*\rho_{\T_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,\cdot)$ is bounded by Beta-type time factors times $\rho_0^{y,\cdot}(t,x-y)$.
conclusions: \item[(1)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for all $0<s<t\le 1$ and $x,y \in \R^d$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d} \rho_{\T_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\T_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\p \Big[(t-s)^{\T_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A(x)\}}\big)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\T_1} s^{\T_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\T_1+[({\beta_1}/{\A(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1=\A(x)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\T_1}s^{\T_2+({\beta_2}/{\A(y)})\wedge 1 -1} \big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_2=\A(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for every $x,y \in \R^d$ and $0<s<t\le 1$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d} \rho_{\T_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\T_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\p \Big[(t-s)^{\T_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\T_1} s^{\T_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_1+\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\T_1+[({\beta_1}/{\A_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\T_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\I_{\{\B_1=\A_2\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\T_1}s^{\T_2+[({\beta_2}/{\A_2})\wedge 1] -1}\big(1+|\log s|\I_{\{\B_2=\A_2\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 (H\"older continuity of $\nabla p^y$)
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for all $x,x',y\in \R^d$ and $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\le &c_1 \left[\left(t^{-1/\A(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left( \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\A(y))}(t,x)+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\A(y))}(t,x')\right). \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')|$ is controlled by $[(t^{-1/\A(y)}|x-x'|)\wedge1]$ times $\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\A(y))}$ at $x$ and $x'$.
assumptions: There exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for all $x,x',y\in \R^d$ and $t \in (0,1]$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \begin{split} \left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\le &c_1 \left[\left(t^{-1/\A(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left( \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\A(y))}(t,x)+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\A(y))}(t,x')\right). \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.5 (continuity in the frozen parameter: $p^x$ versus $p^y$)
nodes.statement: For every $0<\varepsilon, \theta<\A_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\A_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\A_1}))/2)$, there exist $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)\in(0,1]$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T,\e)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z,w\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} |p^x(t,z)-p^y(t,z)|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z),\end{equation} \begin{equation}\left|\nabla p^x(t,z)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\right|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\A(x))-2\G- ({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left| \LL^w p^x(t,z)- \LL^w p^y(t,z)\right|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z), \end{equation} where $\tilde \rho$ is defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.
nodes.statement_short: $p^x$, $\nabla p^x$ and $\LL^w p^x$ differ from their $p^y$ counterparts by at most $|x-y|^{\B_0}$ times a $\tilde\rho$ profile.
assumptions: For every $0<\varepsilon, \theta<\A_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\A_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\A_1}))/2)$, there exist $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)\in(0,1]$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T,\e)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z,w\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$
conclusions: \begin{equation} |p^x(t,z)-p^y(t,z)|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z),\end{equation} \begin{equation}\left|\nabla p^x(t,z)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\right|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\A(x))-2\G- ({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left| \LL^w p^x(t,z)- \LL^w p^y(t,z)\right|\le c_1|x-y|^{\B_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,z), \end{equation} where $\tilde \rho$ is defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 (approximate conservativeness of $\int p^y(t,x-y)\,dy$)
nodes.statement: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, for any $0<\theta<\B_0^*\A_1/\A_2$ and $0<\G<(\theta/\A_2)\wedge ((\B_0^*/\A_2-\theta/\A_1)/2)$, $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} \bigg|\int_{\R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|\p t+t^{(\B_0^*/{\A_2})-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}. \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}\bigg|\int_{\R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|=0. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: $|\int_{\R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1|\p t+t^{(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-(\T/\A_1)}$, so the integral tends to $1$ uniformly as $t\downarrow0$.
assumptions: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, for any $0<\theta<\B_0^*\A_1/\A_2$ and $0<\G<(\theta/\A_2)\wedge ((\B_0^*/\A_2-\theta/\A_1)/2)$, $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in\R^d$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \bigg|\int_{\R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|\p t+t^{(\B_0^*/{\A_2})-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}. \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \R^d}\bigg|\int_{\R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|=0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 (jump-integral of $\delta_{p^x}-\delta_{p^y}$)
nodes.statement: For every $0<\varepsilon, \theta<\A_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\A_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\A_1}))/2)$, there are constants $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)\in (0,1)$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T,\e)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\A(x)}}\,dz \le c_1\tilde \rho^{x,\B_0}_{-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\tilde \rho$ is defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: The $\LL^x$-type integral of $\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;\cdot)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;\cdot)$ is at most $\tilde \rho^{x,\B_0}_{-2\G-(\T/\A_1)}(t,x-y)$.
assumptions: For every $0<\varepsilon, \theta<\A_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\A_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\A_1}))/2)$, there are constants $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)\in (0,1)$ and $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T,\e)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le R_1$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\A(x)}}\,dz \le c_1\tilde \rho^{x,\B_0}_{-2\G-({\T}/{\A_1})}(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\tilde \rho$ is defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 (bound for $\int_{\R^d}\LL^x p^y(t,x-y)\,dy$)
nodes.statement: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, we have the following two statements. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\A_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\A_1})<\B_0^*/\A_2$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\R^d} \LL^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\le c_1t^{-1+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-({\theta}/{\A_1})}. \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\A_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\A_1})<\B_0^*/\A_2$, the estimate \eqref{p4-2-1} will be replaced by \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\R^d} \LL^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\le c_1\big( t^{-1+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-({\theta}/{\A_1})}+t^{1-{(\A_2/\A_1)}}\big). \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: $|\int \LL^x p^y(t,x-y)\,dy|\le c_1t^{-1+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-(\T/\A_1)}$, with an extra $t^{1-(\A_2/\A_1)}$ term when $\K$ depends on $z$.
assumptions: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, we have the following two statements.
conclusions: \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\A_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\A_1})<\B_0^*/\A_2$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\T)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\R^d} \LL^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\le c_1t^{-1+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-({\theta}/{\A_1})}. \end{equation}

\item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\A_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\A_1})<\B_0^*/\A_2$, the estimate \eqref{p4-2-1} will be replaced by \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\R^d} \LL^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\le c_1\big( t^{-1+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-2\G-({\theta}/{\A_1})}+t^{1-{(\A_2/\A_1)}}\big). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.8 (uniform exit-time estimate)
nodes.statement: There exist constants $R_1,A_0\in (0,1)$ such that for every $r \in (0,R_1)$, \begin{equation} \Pp_x\big(\tau_{B(x,A_0 r)}\le r^{\A(x)}\big)\le {1}/{2},\quad x\in \R^d. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: There are $R_1,A_0\in(0,1)$ with $\Pp_x(\tau_{B(x,A_0 r)}\le r^{\A(x)})\le 1/2$ for all $r\in(0,R_1)$ and all $x$.
assumptions: There exist constants $R_1,A_0\in (0,1)$ such that for every $r \in (0,R_1)$
conclusions: \begin{equation} \Pp_x\big(\tau_{B(x,A_0 r)}\le r^{\A(x)}\big)\le {1}/{2},\quad x\in \R^d. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.5 (global upper bounds for $q_0$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose $\K(x,z) =\K (x)$ is independent of $z$. Then for any $\gamma>0$, there exist constants $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K, \G)\in(0,1)$ and $c_0:=c_0(\A,\K, \G)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le &c_0\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{t^{-\gamma}}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x-y|< R_0,\\ \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y|\ge R_0 \end{cases}\\ \p& \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).\end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, \G, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{1}{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y_0|\ge r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\K (x, z)$ and for any $\gamma>0$, there are constants $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K, \G)\in(0,1)$ and $c_0:=c_0(\A,\K, \G)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le& c_0\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{t^{-\gamma}}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x-y|< R_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}}, &|x-y|\ge R_0 \end{cases}\\ \p&\rho_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).\end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y_0|\ge r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $|q_0(t,x,y)|\p\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)$ for $z$-free $\K$ and $\p\rho_{1-(\A_2/\A_1)-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}$ in general, with the $t$-singularity removed where $\A$ is locally constant.
conclusions: \item[(1)] Suppose $\K(x,z) =\K (x)$ is independent of $z$. Then for any $\gamma>0$, there exist constants $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K, \G)\in(0,1)$ and $c_0:=c_0(\A,\K, \G)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le &c_0\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{t^{-\gamma}}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x-y|< R_0,\\ \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y|\ge R_0 \end{cases}\\ \p& \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).\end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, \G, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{1}{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y_0|\ge r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] For general $\K (x, z)$ and for any $\gamma>0$, there are constants $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K, \G)\in(0,1)$ and $c_0:=c_0(\A,\K, \G)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le& c_0\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{t^{-\gamma}}{(t^{{1/\A(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\A(y)}},& |x-y|< R_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}}, &|x-y|\ge R_0 \end{cases}\\ \p&\rho_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).\end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\le c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\A(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\A(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&|x-y_0|\ge r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.8 (pointwise upper bounds for $q_0$ without $\gamma$-loss)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] Suppose $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}}+ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A(y)}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\A(y)}} \end{cases}\\ &\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}. \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Suppose $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\B_0}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_2t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad &|x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1 t^{1-(\A_2/\A_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad & |x-y| > t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Alternative $q_0$ bounds: $t^{-1-d/\A(y)}$ near the diagonal and $|x-y|^{-d-\A(x)}+|x-y|^{-d-\A(y)}$ off it.
conclusions: \item [(1)] Suppose $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}}+ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A(y)}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\A(y)}} \end{cases}\\ &\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}. \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] Suppose $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\B_0}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_2t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad &|x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1 t^{1-(\A_2/\A_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad & |x-y| > t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.9 (H\"older continuity of $q_0$ in $x$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)=\K (x) $ is independent of $z$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ with $\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\A_2}$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, \G, \theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\le c_1\left(|x-x'|^{\A_1(\B_0-\A_2\theta)/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad \times\Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\B_0}/{\A(x)})}\right)(t,x-y) +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\B_0}/{\A(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x-y) +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\K (x, z)$, if $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<{\B_0}/{\A_2}$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $ ({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\gamma =:\G_2 <\theta<{\B_0}/{\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} & |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\le c_2\left(|x-x'|^{\A_1(\B_0-\A_2\theta)/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right) \Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\G_2-({\B_0}/{\A(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\G_2 -({\B_0}/{\A(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y) +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }(t,x-y)\\ & \qquad \quad +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|$ is bounded by $|x-x'|^{\A_1(\B_0-\A_2\theta)/\A(x)}$ times a sum of $\rho$ profiles at $x$ and $x'$.
conclusions: \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)=\K (x) $ is independent of $z$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ with $\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\A_2}$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K, \G, \theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\le c_1\left(|x-x'|^{\A_1(\B_0-\A_2\theta)/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad \times\Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\B_0}/{\A(x)})}\right)(t,x-y) +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\B_0}/{\A(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x-y) +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] For general $\K (x, z)$, if $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<{\B_0}/{\A_2}$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $ ({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\gamma =:\G_2 <\theta<{\B_0}/{\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} & |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\le c_2\left(|x-x'|^{\A_1(\B_0-\A_2\theta)/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right) \Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\G_2-({\B_0}/{\A(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2}+\rho^{y,\B_0}_{\theta-\G_2 -({\B_0}/{\A(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y) +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }(t,x-y)\\ & \qquad \quad +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\I_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\G_2 }(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 3.4 (existence, upper bounds and H\"older continuity of $q$)
nodes.statement: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2})$ and $\B_0^{**} \in (0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2})$. Then, the following two statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent on $(0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d$, it solves equation \eqref{eq2-2} and satisfies that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta^*_0}/{\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le c_1\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\B_0^*/\A_2)}-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0^*}_{-\gamma}\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\B_0^*<\A(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\le & c_1\left(|x-x'|^{{\A_1(\B^*_0-\A_2\theta)}/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\times\Big[\Big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)} (t,x-y)+\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+ (\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for any $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then there is a constant $c_3:=c_3(\A,\K,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\le c_3\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{{\B_0^*/\A_2}}+\rho^{y_0,\B_0^*}_{0}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<{\B^{**}_0}/{\A_2}$ holds true, then $q(t,x,y)=:\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is still absolutely convergent, solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}, and satisfies that for every $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\gamma =:\G_2<\theta<{\B_0^{**}/\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K, \G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le c_2\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\B_0^{**}/\A_2)}-\G_2 }+\rho^{y,\B_0^{**}}_{-\G_2 }\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\B_0^*<\A(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)| &\le c_2\left(|x-x'|^{{\A_1(\B_0^*-\A_2\theta)}/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad\times \Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2+(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x-y) +\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 +(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} If additionally there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$, then there is a constant $c_4:=c_4(\A,\K, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\le c_4\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})+{(\B_0^{**}/\A_2)}}+\rho^{y_0,\B_0^{**}}_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $q=\sum_n q_n$ converges absolutely, solves the Volterra equation, and satisfies $\rho$-type bounds plus a H\"older estimate in $x$.
assumptions: Let $\B_0^*\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2})$ and $\B_0^{**} \in (0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2})$. Then, the following two statements hold.
conclusions: \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent on $(0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d$, it solves equation \eqref{eq2-2} and satisfies that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta^*_0}/{\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le c_1\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\B_0^*/\A_2)}-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\B_0^*}_{-\gamma}\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\B_0^*<\A(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\le & c_1\left(|x-x'|^{{\A_1(\B^*_0-\A_2\theta)}/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\times\Big[\Big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)} (t,x-y)+\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+ (\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for any $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then there is a constant $c_3:=c_3(\A,\K,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\le c_3\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{{\B_0^*/\A_2}}+\rho^{y_0,\B_0^*}_{0}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation}

\item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<{\B^{**}_0}/{\A_2}$ holds true, then $q(t,x,y)=:\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is still absolutely convergent, solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}, and satisfies that for every $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\gamma =:\G_2<\theta<{\B_0^{**}/\A_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K, \G,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d\times \R^d \times \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le c_2\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\B_0^{**}/\A_2)}-\G_2 }+\rho^{y,\B_0^{**}}_{-\G_2 }\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\B_0^*<\A(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)| &\le c_2\left(|x-x'|^{{\A_1(\B_0^*-\A_2\theta)}/{\A(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad\times \Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2+(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x-y) +\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 +(\B_0^{*}/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} If additionally there are some $y_0\in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$, then there is a constant $c_4:=c_4(\A,\K, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\le c_4\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})+{(\B_0^{**}/\A_2)}}+\rho^{y_0,\B_0^{**}}_{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 3.5 (pointwise upper bounds for $q$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_5:=c_5(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_5t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, and $\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then exists a constant $c_6:=c_6(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_6t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Three-regime bound for $|q|$: $t^{-1-d/\A(y)}$, $|x-y|^{-d-\A_2}$ and $|x-y|^{-d-\A_1}$, with an extra $t^{1-\A_2/\A_1}$ when $\K$ depends on $z$.
conclusions: \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_5:=c_5(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_5t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$, and $\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then exists a constant $c_6:=c_6(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\le \begin{cases} c_6t^{-1-({d}/{\A(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\le t^{{1}/{\A(y)}},\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.1 (well-definedness and first upper bounds for $p$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma,c_0>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d/\A(x)}}, & |y-x|\le c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\G}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},& c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |y-x|\le R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|y-x|> R_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} Suppose additionally that there are some $x_0 \in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} \frac{c_2 t }{(t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}+|x_0-y|)^{d+\A(x_0)}},& |x_0-y|\le {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\G} }{|x_0-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|x_0-y|>{r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<\min\{{\B_0}/{\A_2},1/2\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases}c_1t^{-{d/\A(x)}}, & |y-x|\le c_0 t^{{1/\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\G}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},& c_0 t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |y-x|\le R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\G }}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|y-x|> R_0, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\tilde\G:=({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\G$. Suppose additionally there exist some $x_0 \in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,r_0,c_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} {c_2}{t^{-{d/\A (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{2-{(\A_2/\A_1)}} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\A(x_0)}},& \quad c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}\le |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\tilde\G} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\ge {r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The Levi series defines $p$ and gives upper bounds $t^{-d/\A(x)}$, $t^{1-\G}|x-y|^{-d-\A(x)}$, $t^{1-\gamma}|x-y|^{-d-\A_1}$.
conclusions: \item[(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma,c_0>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d/\A(x)}}, & |y-x|\le c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\G}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},& c_0t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |y-x|\le R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|y-x|> R_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} Suppose additionally that there are some $x_0 \in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} \frac{c_2 t }{(t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}+|x_0-y|)^{d+\A(x_0)}},& |x_0-y|\le {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\G} }{|x_0-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|x_0-y|>{r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1<\min\{{\B_0}/{\A_2},1/2\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\A,\K,\G,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases}c_1t^{-{d/\A(x)}}, & |y-x|\le c_0 t^{{1/\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\G}}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}},& c_0 t^{{1/\A(x)}}\le |y-x|\le R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\G }}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},&|y-x|> R_0, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\tilde\G:=({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1+\G$. Suppose additionally there exist some $x_0 \in \R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,r_0,c_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\le \begin{cases} {c_2}{t^{-{d/\A (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{2-{(\A_2/\A_1)}} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\A(x_0)}},& \quad c_0t^{{1/\A(x_0)}}\le |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\tilde\G} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\A_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\ge {r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.3 (sharp-in-$t$ upper bounds for $p$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\le c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& c_0 t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item [(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\B_0^{**}}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_2t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\le c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bounds with the optimal linear factor $t$ (resp. $t^{2-\A_2/\A_1}$): $t|x-y|^{-d-\A_2}$ for $|x-y|\le1$ and $t|x-y|^{-d-\A_1}$ beyond.
conclusions: \item [(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\le c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& c_0 t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation}

\item [(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\B_0^{**}}/{\A_2}>({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\le \begin{cases} c_2t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\le c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_2}},\quad& c_0t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}< |x-y| \le 1,\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\A_2}/{\A_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\A_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.6 (H\"older regularity of $p(t,\cdot,y)$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then, for every $\G>0$ small enough, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\le c_1 |x-x'|^{(\A(x)-\G)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\G/(2\A_2)}}(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{{\G/(2\A_2)}}(t,x'-y)\big). \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}$, then for every $\G>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|\le& c_1|x-x'|^{(\A_1-\G)_+\wedge 1}\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\G_1 }(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\G_1 }(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\G_1:=1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})+({\G}/({2\A_2}))$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then, for every $\G>0$ small enough, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\le c_1 |x-x'|^{(\A(x)-\G)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\G/(2\A_2)}}(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{{\G/(2\A_2)}}(t,x'-y)\big). \end{split} \end{equation}

\item[(2)] Let $\B_0^{**}\in(0,\B_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/{\A_2}$, then for every $\G>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\A,\K,\G)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \R^d$ with $|x-x'|\le R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|\le& c_1|x-x'|^{(\A_1-\G)_+\wedge 1}\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\G_1 }(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\G_1 }(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\G_1:=1-({\A_2}/{\A_1})+({\G}/({2\A_2}))$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.7 (differentiability and gradient estimate of $p(t,\cdot,y)$ at $x_0$)
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Let $\B_0^*:=\B_0\wedge\A_2$. If $\tilde \B_0(x_0):=({\A_1\B_0}/{\A(x_0)})\wedge\A_1>1-\A(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. Moreover, for every $\G>0$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_1\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\A(x_0)})+(\B_0^*/\A_2)- (\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G}(t,x_0-y) \end{equation} holds for some $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,x_0)>0$. \item[(2)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/\A_2$, where $\B_0^{**}:=\B_0\wedge (\A_2/2)$. If $\tilde \B_0(x_0) -({\A_1\A_2}/{\A(x_0)})(({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1)>1-\A_1$ for some $x_0\in \R^d$ with $\tilde \B_0(x_0)$ defined in $(i)$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \R^d$. Furthermore, for every $\G>0$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,x_0)>0$ such that \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_2\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1}/{\A_1})+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G_2 }(t,x_0-y), \end{equation} where $\G_2 :={(\A_2/\A_1)}-1+\G$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: If $\tilde \B_0(x_0)>1-\A(x_0)$ then $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0$ with a $\rho$-type gradient bound depending only on $\A(x_0)$.
conclusions: \item[(1)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Let $\B_0^*:=\B_0\wedge\A_2$. If $\tilde \B_0(x_0):=({\A_1\B_0}/{\A(x_0)})\wedge\A_1>1-\A(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. Moreover, for every $\G>0$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_1\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\A(x_0)})+(\B_0^*/\A_2)- (\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G}(t,x_0-y) \end{equation} holds for some $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K,\G,x_0)>0$.

\item[(2)] Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/\A_2$, where $\B_0^{**}:=\B_0\wedge (\A_2/2)$. If $\tilde \B_0(x_0) -({\A_1\A_2}/{\A(x_0)})(({\A_2}/{\A_1})-1)>1-\A_1$ for some $x_0\in \R^d$ with $\tilde \B_0(x_0)$ defined in $(i)$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \R^d$. Furthermore, for every $\G>0$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\A,\K,\G,x_0)>0$ such that \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\le c_2\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1}/{\A_1})+(\B_0^*/\A_2)-(\B_0^*/\A_1)-\G_2 }(t,x_0-y), \end{equation} where $\G_2 :={(\A_2/\A_1)}-1+\G$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.9 (joint continuity of $p$)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, or that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/\A_2$, where $\B_0^{**}:=\B_0\wedge (\A_2/2)$. Then, $p:(0,1]\times\R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ is continuous.
nodes.statement_short: $p:(0,1]\times\R^d\times\R^d\to\R_+$ is continuous.
assumptions: Suppose that $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, or that $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\B_0^{**}/\A_2$, where $\B_0^{**}:=\B_0\wedge (\A_2/2)$.
conclusions: Then, $p:(0,1]\times\R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ is continuous.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.4 ($p$ solves the parabolic equation pointwise)
nodes.statement: The following two statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ defined by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise. \item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\min\{{\B_0}/{\A_2},{1}/{2}\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ also satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: The function $p$ built by the Levi ansatz satisfies $\partial_t p(t,x,y)=\LL p(t,\cdot,y)(x)$ pointwise.
assumptions: The following two statements hold.
conclusions: \item [(1)] If $\K(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ defined by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise.
\item[(2)] If $\K(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\A_2/\A_1)}-1<\min\{{\B_0}/{\A_2},{1}/{2}\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ also satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.6 (on-diagonal lower bounds)
nodes.statement: There exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le 5 (t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\A(y)}})$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y) \ge c_1t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: Near the diagonal $|x-y|\le 5(t^{1/\A(x)}\vee t^{1/\A(y)})$ one has $p(t,x,y)\ge c_1t^{-d/\A(x)}$.
assumptions: There exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \R^d$ with $|x-y|\le 5 (t^{{1}/{\A(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\A(y)}})$
conclusions: \begin{equation} p(t,x,y) \ge c_1t^{-{d}/{\A(x)}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 5.7 (associated strong Markov process and its L\'evy system)
nodes.statement: $(1)$ There is a strong Markov process $X:=\big((X_t)_{t \ge 0}; (\Pp_x)_{x\in \R^d}\big)$ such that for every $f \in C_b^2(\R^d)$, \begin{equation} M_t^f:=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t \LL f(X_s)\,ds,\quad t \in (0,1] \end{equation} is a martingale with respect to the natural filtration $\mathscr{F}_t:=\sigma\{X_s,0\le s\le t\}$ under probability measure $\Pp_x$ for all $x \in \R^d$. Moreover, $X$ has the strong Feller property. $(2)$ For every non-negative measurable function $g:(0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ vanishing on $\{(s,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d: x=y\}$ and any stopping time $T$, we have \begin{equation} \Ee_x\left(\sum_{s \le T\wedge 1}g(s,X_{s-},X_s)\right)=\Ee_x \bigg(\int_0^{T\wedge 1}\int_{\R^d} g(s,X_s,y)J(X_s,y)\,dy\,ds\bigg), \end{equation} where $$J(x,y):=\frac{\K(x,y-x)}{|y-x|^{d+\A(x)}},\quad x,y \in \R^d.$$
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
nodes.statement_short: There is a strong Markov process $X$ solving the martingale problem for $\LL$, having the strong Feller property, with L\'evy system given by $J(x,y)$.
assumptions: for every $f \in C_b^2(\R^d)$
For every non-negative measurable function $g:(0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ vanishing on $\{(s,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d: x=y\}$ and any stopping time $T$
conclusions: There is a strong Markov process $X:=\big((X_t)_{t \ge 0}; (\Pp_x)_{x\in \R^d}\big)$ such that for every $f \in C_b^2(\R^d)$, \begin{equation} M_t^f:=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t \LL f(X_s)\,ds,\quad t \in (0,1] \end{equation} is a martingale with respect to the natural filtration $\mathscr{F}_t:=\sigma\{X_s,0\le s\le t\}$ under probability measure $\Pp_x$ for all $x \in \R^d$. Moreover, $X$ has the strong Feller property. $(2)$ For every non-negative measurable function $g:(0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d \rightarrow \R_+$ vanishing on $\{(s,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \R^d \times \R^d: x=y\}$ and any stopping time $T$, we have \begin{equation} \Ee_x\left(\sum_{s \le T\wedge 1}g(s,X_{s-},X_s)\right)=\Ee_x \bigg(\int_0^{T\wedge 1}\int_{\R^d} g(s,X_s,y)J(X_s,y)\,dy\,ds\bigg), \end{equation} where $$J(x,y):=\frac{\K(x,y-x)}{|y-x|^{d+\A(x)}},\quad x,y \in \R^d.$$

nodes.name: Proposition 5.9 (off-diagonal lower bound estimates)
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$ with $|x-y|>5\max\{t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}\}$ \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\ge \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Existence and Uniqueness of the Solution
assumptions: There exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\A,\K)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\R^d$ with $|x-y|>5\max\{t^{{1}/{\A(x)}},t^{{1}/{\A(y)}}\}$
conclusions: \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\ge \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\A(x)}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Corollary 3.2 (time-integrated convolution inequality with Beta factor)
nodes.statement: Let $\Bb(\gamma,\beta)$ denote the Beta function with respect to $\gamma$ and $\beta$.
